## Summary

I imported and diffed the `Epics.html` design (claude.ai/design project `0ca33cd3-c2fa-4644-b728-bde42292abbd`) against the current app. The two-pane Epics workspace it describes (queue + detail, search/filter/group/sort/pin/paging/keyboard nav, Chat⇄Terminal toggle, Discussion/PRDs/Runs tabs, the rich Turn renderer) was **already fully implemented** in a prior session (PRDs 827/828/829/831/833/837) — my earlier reading of `EpicComposer.tsx`/`EpicDetail.tsx`/`EpicQueue.tsx` confirmed this before I touched anything.

The remote design had moved on since that sync, adding a per-row overflow menu (rename/edit-goal/pin/mark-completed/duplicate/resume-in-terminal/copy-id/delete) plus a Composer quote-reply affordance and an 8-situation Turn split (`epic-thread.jsx`). I:

1. **Implemented the safe subset now**, in `src/renderer/components/epics/EpicQueue.tsx`: a `RowMenuButton`/`RowMenu` overflow menu offering **Copy Epic ID**, **Mark completed**, and **Resume in terminal** — all backed by existing store actions, no new persistence. Typecheck, `lint:selectors`, and all 72 existing Epics unit tests pass.
2. **Filed proposed Epic** `epic-queue-row-actions-rename-duplicate-delete-63b84dd6` for the remainder (rename/edit-goal/duplicate/delete) — these need new store+IPC mutations that must respect the single-writer law and the already-fragile active-index.json write serialization, so I scoped that as real design work rather than rushing it into this pass.
3. **Refreshed the local design-mock docs** (`design-mocks/epics/epics-mock.jsx`, new `epic-thread-mock.jsx`, `DESIGN_SPEC.md`) so the next sync has an accurate baseline, and explicitly noted that `ChatTranscriptTurn.tsx` already covers the mock's 8 Turn situations against real data (not a gap) — the one genuine small gap is Composer quote-reply, not yet filed as its own Epic.
Did you also implement all the action buttons, varios modals and options? Every change and button both UI and API paths and tested?

No — I scoped this deliberately, and not everything is done. Here's the honest breakdown:

**What I implemented (UI + wired to real store/API paths, but no new tests written for it):**
- Row overflow menu (`RowMenuButton`/`RowMenu` in `EpicQueue.tsx`) with 3 actions:
  - **Copy Epic ID** — pure clipboard, no backend.
  - **Mark completed** — calls the *existing* `usePromptSessions().markCompleted` action (same one `EpicDetail`'s button already used).
  - **Resume in terminal** — calls the *existing* `useEpicTerminal().setMode` action.
- These reuse pre-existing, already-tested store/IPC paths. I did **not** write new unit tests for the menu component itself (no test asserts the menu opens, positions, or that each item fires its handler) — I only confirmed the pre-existing 72 Epics tests still pass, which they would regardless of whether the new menu code is correct, since none of them exercise it.

**What I explicitly did NOT implement (real gaps, not oversights):**
1. **Rename title / Edit goal (inline RowEditor)** — no button, no modal, no store mutation. `PromptSession` has no title/goal-patch action today.
2. **Duplicate as new Epic** — not implemented. No mutation exists.
3. **Delete Epic** — not implemented. Destructive, no confirm modal, no precedent in this codebase.
4. **Reopen** (for a completed Epic from the queue row) — not implemented; only `markCompleted` (one direction) is wired.
5. **Composer quote-reply** (TUser's hover "Quote" → reply-context strip in the composer) — not implemented at all, not even filed as its own Epic yet.

Items 1–4 are filed as proposed Epic `epic-queue-row-actions-rename-duplicate-delete-63b84dd6` (requires new store+IPC mutations respecting the single-writer law — I judged that unsafe to rush). Item 5 (quote-reply) is a real gap I flagged in the docs but have not yet filed.

**On "tested":** typecheck, `lint:selectors`, and the existing 72 Epics unit tests pass — but that only proves I didn't break anything pre-existing. No new automated test covers the 3 menu actions I added, and I did not manually drive the app in a browser/Electron window to click the new menu and verify it renders/positions/fires correctly. That verification is still outstanding.

All four carry the mandatory test/security AC inline (per `standards.md`, not spun into separate PRDs) and point the headless executor at `standards.md`'s absolute path. You can watch them in the Scheduler tab, or run them now via "Run now" — **I cannot poll or report back on their progress myself**, since this is a one-shot session that ends when I stop writing.

**On your second ask** — "make sure that this is the starting grounding for EPICs of type Feature and Bug" — I did not queue anything for this because I genuinely can't tell which of these you mean, and guessing wrong means real rework:
- (a) Make the Epics-workspace *design* (this row-menu/queue UI) the template every new **Feature**- and **Bug**-tagged Epic gets, as opposed to Discussion-tagged ones (e.g. hide certain actions for Discussion Epics)?
- (b) Make `DESIGN_SPEC.md`/this design sync the canonical reference doc that any future Feature/Bug PRD authoring must ground itself in (a documentation/process rule, not a UI change)?
- (c) Something about how a **new** Feature or Bug Epic is seeded/scaffolded at creation time (e.g. `NewEpicCard.tsx` pre-filling something from this design) — "starting grounding" as in its initial state?

I mean that starting  Bug or Feature we know there will be development and decomposition of PRDS. Starting a discussion it is not clear if we yet need to do the develop so it should stay as a skill available to the agent but not jumped into right away

## Summary

Matched `EpicComposer.tsx`'s prompt panel to your screenshot:

- **Merged the two header rows into one**, matching the screenshot exactly: `[Chat | Dispatch as PRD]` toggle → `in` → status dot + Epic title, all on a single line (was previously a separate "iterating in..." row above the toggle row).
- **Added a folder/attach icon button** next to the mic button inside the joined input-tools box (with a divider), wired to the same `att.add(...)` attachment flow — this was a real gap: `DESIGN_SPEC.md` already documented "mic + attach in a joined button group" but the attach half was never built.
- **Suppressed the full-width dashed drop-zone when empty** (new `hideZoneWhenEmpty` prop on the shared `AttachTray`, opt-in so `NewEpicCard`'s own usage is untouched) — it only appears once there are actual attachment chips to show, matching the clean single-row look in the screenshot instead of always showing "Paste a screenshot... / Attach".
- **Shortened the running placeholder** to `"Queue a follow-up…"` to match the screenshot text exactly.
- **Added a send/paper-plane icon** to the Send/Queue button, matching the screenshot's icon+label button.

Fixed one test that broke as a side effect (it queried the AttachTray's now-conditionally-hidden file input; retargeted it to the new dedicated `epic-composer-attach-input`). `npm run typecheck`, `check-unstable-selectors`, and the full epics test suite (94 tests) all pass. This was small, contained, directly-requested visual work, done inline per `developer_sg.md`'s "user explicitly says to do it inline right now" exception — nothing queued to the scheduler for this pass.
